ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, if \( Z \) is an inductive reactance, what is the phase relationship between the voltage across \( Z \) and the current through it?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Diagram description: In the attached figure, the arrow of current i is drawn on the upper wire, directed to the right, entering the upper end of the right-side vertical element Z; the reference polarity of voltage U is marked on the left side, with the upper end as + and the lower end as -, corresponding to the two ends of Z, namely the upper end is positive and the lower end is negative. Therefore the voltage and current use the passive sign convention. Reasoning: The problem states that Z is inductive reactance, namely Z = jX_L. Under the passive sign convention, the voltage phasor U = ZI = jX_L I. Multiplication by j means that the voltage phasor leads the current phasor by 90°. Therefore the voltage across the two ends of Z leads the current passing through it.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, if \( Z \) is an inductive reactance, what is the phase relationship between the voltage across \( Z \) and the current through it?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify that current i enters the top terminal of the element Z, while the voltage U is referenced with + at the top and - at the bottom, so voltage and current use the passive sign convention. From the text, take that Z is specifically an inductive reactance. Apply the inductor phasor relation V = jX_L I; therefore the voltage across Z leads the current through Z by 90 degrees. Answer: voltage leads current.
